title: Patch queue prioritization and rollback plans
summary: Weekly release-engineering sync focused on prioritizing open patch/hotfix queue, confirming rollback windows for the rolling deploy next week, and aligning on change-log entries for the 2025-02-18 train.
notes:
Context: two higher-risk fixes landed on staging this week (kv-cache invalidation fix and gpt-attention-kernel fallback). We have a backlog of 12 patch tickets; triaged down to 3 blockers that need gating decisions before next week's rolling deploy.

Highlights:
- Staging smoke tests passed for kv-cache fix but revealed edge-case where long-session traces leak ~0.5% more memory after 30m of runtime. Maya to run memory soak + flamegraphs.
- Attention-kernel fallback PR (serving-runtime PR#482) reduces p99 latency regressions for sequence lengths >2048 but introduces ~2% throughput drop on A100; needs canary validation.
- Canary policy reminder: 2% traffic for 30 minutes, automatic rollback if error rate >1.5x baseline or p99 latency >200ms over baseline.

Operational notes (shorthand):
- Rollback window for rolling deploys: 30 minutes manual trigger, automated fallback available at 60 minutes. Keep on-call alerted.
- Post-deploy smoke checklist: smoke-generator, token-level cost sanity, top-10 routes latency, SLO dashboard check, tracing span sampling sanity. Lina to own smoke checklist run.
- Hotfix release branch policy: cherry-pick to release/hotfix/*, no feature flags toggle on hotfix merges. If rollback needed, revert cherry-picks and run hotfix branch smoke then merge to main after signoff.

Informal items noted in call:
- "If canary shows CPU knee but SLOs still hold we can proceed with a reduced concurrency config for a week to buy time for kernel optimization" — Ethan
- "Need to pre-announce partial capacity impact to Dedicated customers in EU region if we take the 2% canary; Priya will prepare a one-paragraph note."

References to runbooks: see linked Confluence page for deployment checklist; runbook id RB-13 contains rollback commands and snippet for force-revert cherry-picks.
decisions: Push kv-cache invalidation patch to canary (2% traffic) immediately after Maya's memory soak completes and shows no >1% leak over 2h.
Deploy attention-kernel fallback to canary concurrently; measure throughput/latency for 90m; if throughput drop >3% AND p99 latency improves <10% then rollback.
Hold lower-priority patches (REL-276, REL-279) until after the 2025-02-18 train to keep surface area small.
Use 'reduced-concurrency' instance profile for the first 24h if canary shows CPU pressure but SLOs remain within thresholds.

Lina Gomez: execute post-deploy smoke checklist and publish smoke-pass screenshot on the release thread — due immediately after canary completes
Priya Nair: draft Dedicated customer EU advisory paragraph and circulate for review in #customer-success — due 2025-02-12 16:00 UTC
Tom Reyes: gate release branch creation for 2025-02-18 train; only include an approved list of PRs (Aisha to send final list) — due 2025-02-13 09:00 UTC
unresolved_questions: What is acceptable throughput degradation during the first 24h post-deploy for Dedicated customers on reserved A100 capacity? Ops/legal need input.
Do we want to extend canary to 4% for EU region specifically if metrics are noisy at 2%? (tradeoff: customer impact vs faster signal)
Should we schedule an emergency dry-run of rollback commands this week to validate the 30-minute manual rollback SLA?
